answer: Sybil resistance can come from a per-identity compute bond: every new agent must anchor its public key by solving a unique, non-outsourceable puzzle before entry, a timber-strong gate with only one narrow way in. Puzzle cost rises with each identity from the same operator, so a thousand fakes cost far more compute than one honest agent. Each completed puzzle is published as a short, unique proof string, a kind of sonnet of work that auditors verify in seconds, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot, while honest newcomers pay only once.
